newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to deport foreign workers marrying locals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to deport foreign workers marrying locals.

text.p: Unskilled male foreign workers with six-month work permits will be deported if they marry Malaysian women, Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob was quoted as saying by The Star newspaper on Thursday.
The ruling would be enforced immediately for short-term foreign workers in blue-collar sectors such as construction sites and plantations, he told reporters.

"The Cabinet has decided that the permits of foreign workers who marry local women, including 'orang asli' (Malaysian aborigines), be immediately revoked and they will be directed to leave the country with their Malaysian wives," Megat Junid was quoted as saying.
He said the move was to prevent "marriages of convenience", with the foreign workers seeing the marriages as "tickets to work permits, citizenship and other benefits open only to Malaysian citizens".
He did not give any figures of mariages between foreign workers and Malaysians.
Malaysia has more than 1.2 million foreign workers out of a total workforce of around eight million.
Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said last week Malaysia was reviewing its foreign worker recruitment policy in an effort to curb resulting social problems.
Recent fights and tension between villagers and Bangladeshi workers have been highlighted in the media in recent weeks.
The worst incident took place on September 10 when seven Bangladeshi workers were seriously injured in a fight involving 70 Bangladeshis and dozens of villagers in southern Johor state.
Bangladeshi State Minister for Foreign Affairs Abul Hasan Chowdhury, in Malaysia with a trade delegation, said most Bangladeshi workers were responsible people.

"I've discussed this with the Malaysian officials and we agreed that the majority of Bangladeshi workers here are hardworking, meticulous, responsible and contribute significantly to the economy," he was quoted as saying in The Star.
